title: Dissecting Agentic Forensics: The Role of Triage, Prompting, and Evidence Arbitration in Open-World Fake Image Detection
abstract: arXiv:2609.24359v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Image forensics is increasingly an open-world problem: manipulations range from fully synthetic images to localized edits, splicing and swapping, while most forensic detectors remain specialized to a single manipulation family. Agentic AI has recently emerged as a promising solution. In principle, such systems can assess the reliability of individual detectors, identify out-of-scope evidence, and arbitrate conflicting reports. However, it remains unclear which components actually drive performance and whether their benefits persist under distribution shift. To answer these questions, we study a training-free agentic framework built around specialist detectors, per-detector triage, and conflict-aware evidence arbitration. Using six configurations and three multimodal large language model backbones, we dissect the role of triage, prompting, and reasoning quality on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution data. translated_abstract: 图像取证日益成为一个开放世界问题：篡改手段涵盖从完全合成的图像到局部编辑、拼接与替换，而大多数取证检测器仍局限于单一篡改类型。智能体AI近来作为一种有前景的解决方案出现。原则上，这类系统可以评估单个检测器的可靠性、识别超出范围的证据，并仲裁相互冲突的报告。然而，目前尚不清楚哪些组件真正驱动了性能，以及它们的优势在分布偏移下是否仍然存在。为了回答这些问题，我们研究了一个免训练的智能体框架，该框架围绕专家检测器、逐检测器分诊和冲突感知的证据仲裁构建。通过六种配置和三个多模态大语言模型骨干，我们剖析了分诊、提示和推理质量在分布内和分布外数据上的作用。我们的结果表明……
tldr: 该论文通过一个免训练的智能体取证框架，系统剖析了分诊、提示与冲突感知的证据仲裁等组件在开放世界伪造图像检测中对分布内和分布外性能的实际贡献。
en_tdlr: This paper dissects a training-free agentic forensics framework to reveal how triage, prompting, and conflict-aware evidence arbitration drive performance in open-world fake image detection under both in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings.
